chapters.title: Keyumars — The First King
chapters.summary: Before any king sits the throne, Ferdowsi opens with God — the God of Soul and Wisdom. Creation unfolds: light from darkness, sun and moon set to their paths, humanity given kherad. Then from the sacred peaks of Pars, Keyumars rises as the first king.
chapters.story: Ferdowsi opens not with a throne but with wisdom — 'be nam-e Khoda-vand-e jan o kherad'. The cosmos is built: light separates from darkness, sun and moon begin their eternal paths, and humanity alone receives the gift of kherad. From this philosophical foundation, Keyumars rises on the sacred mountains of Pars. He wears leopard skin; the beasts bow. He teaches the first laws of civilization. But Ahriman, lord of the dark, sends his Black Div down through the smoke to break the first dawn before it can bloom. Siamak falls. The first sorrow enters the world.
chapters.summary_fa: پیش از هر شاهی، فردوسی با خدا می‌گشاید — خداوندِ جان و خرد. کیومرث از کوه‌های مقدسِ پارس برمی‌خیزد. نخستین قانون‌های تمدن. بعد اهریمن از دود پایین می‌فرستد و سیامک می‌افتد. نخستین غم داخلِ دنیا می‌شود.
chapters.summary_tg: Пеш аз ҳар подшоҳе, Фирдавсӣ бо Худо мекушояд. Киюмарс аз кӯҳҳои муқаддаси Порс бармехезад. Аввалин қонунҳои тамаддун. Баъд Аҳриман аз дуд фуруд меояд ва Сиёмак меафтад.

chapters.title: Hushang — The Spark of Fire
chapters.summary: Hushang strikes flint at a serpent and instead wakes the eternal flame. Sade, the festival of fire, is born.
chapters.story: Hushang the wise grandson struck flint at a serpent of black scales. The stone missed, but a spark leapt up and a tree caught fire. From that night the people knew flame, and Hushang named the festival Sade. Iron was forged. Water was led to fields. The first crafts were taught to humankind.
chapters.summary_fa: هوشنگ با چخماق به ماری می‌زند. سنگ خطا می‌کند، اما جرقه‌ای برجهید و درختی آتش گرفت. از آن شب مردم آتش شناختند. آهن آب شد. آب به کشتزار رفت.
chapters.summary_tg: Ҳушанг бо чахмоқ ба мор мезанад. Санг хато мекунад, аммо ҷарақае парид ва дарахте сӯхт. Аз он шаб мардум оташ шинохтанд.

chapters.title: Tahmuras — Binder of Demons
chapters.summary: Tahmuras the Div-band rides through smoke and chains the demons. They beg for life and trade their secret: writing.
chapters.story: Tahmuras the Div-band rode through smoke and shadow with a club of cypress. He chained the demons and dragged them to the foot of his throne. To save their lives the demons taught him thirty alphabets — Greek, Tazi, Pahlavi, Sogdian. Knowledge was bought with mercy, and the world remembered.
chapters.summary_fa: تهمورثِ دیوبند با عصایِ سرو از دودوسایه می‌راند. دیوان را در زنجیر می‌کشد. برای جان‌هایشان سی الفبا یاد می‌دهند. دانش با مهربانی خریده شد.
chapters.summary_tg: Таҳмурасти Девбанд аз дуду соя мерондад. Девонро занҷир мезанад. Барои ҷонҳояшон си алифбо меомӯзонанд.

chapters.title: Jamshid — The Golden Throne
chapters.summary: Jamshid divides the people into four crafts and sits a kingdom of crystal. Pride finally outshines the sun.
chapters.story: Jamshid divided the people into four crafts: priests, warriors, farmers, artisans. He raised a crystal throne and was carried into the sky by demons on Nowruz. Three hundred years of light. Then pride: he claimed to be a god, and the divine grace, the farr, departed from him.
chapters.summary_fa: جمشید مردم را به چهار پیشه تقسیم کرد. تختِ بلورین برپا کرد و دیوان به آسمانش بردند. سیصد سالِ روشنایی. بعد غرور: ادعای الوهیت کرد و فرّ از او رفت.
chapters.summary_tg: Ҷамшед мардумро ба чаҳор пеша тақсим кард. Тахти буллӯрин бардошт. Сесад соли равшанӣ. Баъд ғурур: даъвои худоӣ кард ва фарр аз ӯ рафт.

chapters.title: Zahhak — The Serpent King
chapters.summary: Two serpents grow from Zahhak's shoulders. Their daily price is two human brains. A thousand years of darkness.
chapters.story: From the kiss of Iblis, two black serpents sprang from Zahhak's shoulders. Each day demanded two human brains, drawn from the youth of Pars. A thousand years of darkness pressed on the land — until a blacksmith's apron rose as a banner.
chapters.summary_fa: از بوسه‌ی ابلیس دو مارِ سیاه از دوشِ ضحاک رویید. هر روز دو مغزِ انسانی طلبیدند. هزار سالِ تاریکی — تا پیشبندِ آهنگری به عنوانِ درفش برافراشته شد.
chapters.summary_tg: Аз бӯсаи Иблис ду морид аз дӯши Заҳҳок рӯид. Ҳар рӯз ду мағзи инсон талабиданд. Ҳазор соли торикӣ.

chapters.title: Fereydun — The Liberator
chapters.summary: Kaveh the blacksmith raises his apron as a banner. Fereydun's bull-headed mace ends a tyrant.
chapters.story: Kaveh the blacksmith raised his leather apron on a spear, and the people of Pars marched. Fereydun took up the bull-headed mace forged for this hour. Zahhak was bound to Damavand's mountain forever. The kingdom split among Fereydun's three sons: Iraj, Tur, Salm — and from their feud, the Shahnameh's wars began.
chapters.summary_fa: کاوه‌ی آهنگر پیشبندِ چرمینش را بر نیزه برافراشت و مردم پارس راه افتادند. فریدون گرزِ گاوسر گرفت. ضحاک برای همیشه به دماوند بسته شد. پادشاهی میانِ سه پسر تقسیم شد.
chapters.summary_tg: Ковааи Оҳангар пешбандашро бардошт ва мардуми Порс роҳ афтоданд. Фаридун гурзи говсар гирифт. Заҳҳок ба Дамованд бандшуд.

chapters.title: Manuchehr — The Avenger
chapters.summary: From Fereydun's sorrow, a new king rises. Manuchehr avenges Iraj — and a world still shaped by blood begins again.
chapters.story:
Iraj was the youngest of Fereydun's sons and the gentlest. When the world was divided, he asked for Pars — not from greed but from love of his father's memory. His brothers Tur and Salm could not understand a man who genuinely wanted less, and so they killed him. Fereydun received the news and did not weep immediately. He was five hundred years old. He sat alone for three days. On the fourth day he called for Manuchehr — Iraj's grandson — and began the raising that would become a purpose.

Manuchehr grew up knowing what he was for. Every lesson in swordsmanship carried Iraj's name. Every lesson in statecraft carried the question: why did Tur and Salm choose wrong? When the army marched east under the Derafsh Kaviani — the same banner Kaveh had raised against Zahhak — Manuchehr rode at its center. He met Tur in single combat because the debt was personal and the payment had to be personal. When Tur fell, both armies went silent: half from grief, half from relief. Salm fled to his ships and was caught at sea. The blood feud was paid in full.

Fereydun received the news and allowed himself, at last, to grieve — not for the justice but for the sons they were before the choice. He did not live long after. Manuchehr ruled justly, with Sam the Warrior holding the borders as champion. The chronicle paused. But in the far north, Sam's son was already being born with hair as white as Damavand's peak — and the Shahnameh's next great story had already begun.
chapters.summary_fa: ایرج کوچکترین و مهربانترینِ پسرانِ فریدون بود. برادران طوتر و سلم کشتندش. فریدون پانصدساله چهار روز تنها نشست. روزِ چهارم منوچهر را خواند. انتقام شخصی بود و شخصی پرداخته شد.
chapters.summary_tg: Эраҷ хурдтарин ва меҳрубонтарини писарони Фаридун буд. Бародарон куштанд. Манӯчеҳр ба ками рафт ва интиқом гирифт.

chapters.title: Nozar — The Kingdom Divides
chapters.summary: Nozar inherits the throne but not the virtue. The age of great kings dims — and Afrasiab crosses the Oxus.
chapters.story:
Nozar inherited the throne of Manuchehr without inheriting the virtue that held it. He dismissed the old champions who had served under Sam — the warriors who knew the borders and the cold distances of the north. He replaced experience with flattery, and the court grew soft while the frontier grew thin. A king without farr is a king who does not know he is diminishing until the diminishment is complete.

Afrasiab, grandson of the line that Manuchehr had fought, watched from across the Oxus and saw what Nozar could not: that Iran was open. He crossed the river with an army that moved like winter — without the personal debts that had given Manuchehr's war its limits. This was not a blood feud. This was empire. The armies of Iran met the Turanian tide and broke. Nozar was taken alive, and Afrasiab sat briefly on the throne of Iran. The Shahnameh does not celebrate this; it mourns it. A king too weak to hold the farr does not lose only himself — he loses the kingdom for a generation.

Sam's old warriors, fighting under Zav of the survivors' line, drove the invasion back across the Oxus eventually. The throne was recovered. But something had changed. Iran had felt what it meant to lose its center — to have the great chronicle interrupted by a ruler who did not deserve its weight. The wound from this chapter does not close. It widens into the Iran-Turan wars that will shape every chapter for centuries to come, and into which Rostam himself will be born.
chapters.summary_fa: نوذر تخت را بدون فضیلتی که نگهش می‌داشت به ارث برد. فرماندهانِ کهنه را کنار گذاشت. افراسیاب از آنطرفِ جیحون دید. ایران باز بود. شاهی بدون فرّ نمی‌داند که دارد کوچک می‌شود.
chapters.summary_tg: Нӯзар тахтро бе фазилат ба мерос гирифт. Афросиёб аз рӯди Ҷайҳун дид ва ҳамла кард. Эрон даргоҳ буд.

chapters.title: Zal — The Albino Prince
chapters.summary: Born white-haired, cast to the mountain, raised by Simorgh, Zal returns to Pars on wings of myth.
chapters.story:
Sam the warrior — champion of Manuchehr, guardian of Iran's northern borders — had a son. The child was born with hair as white as snow, as white as Damavand's peak. In Sam's world, this was an omen that could only mean one thing: Ahriman's touch. Sam was a celebrated man, a man of courts and kings, and he could not bear to display what the world would read as a curse. He took the infant to Mount Alborz and left him there. The mountain took the child and gave him to the Simorgh.

The Simorgh was no ordinary bird. She was the world's oldest witness — she had watched three destructions of the world from her nest in the world-tree on Alborz. She carried Zal up to her nest and raised him among her chicks, feeding him, teaching him the patience of long years and the knowledge of a creature who has seen everything. Zal grew up not knowing what he was missing: he had feathers, sky, wisdom, and a mother who was older than the first king.

Sam dreamed of a young man on the mountain and woke knowing it was his son and knowing he had been wrong. He rode north, climbed to the nest, and found a prince who was more than a prince. The Simorgh returned Zal with ceremony. She gave him one feather: 'Burn it,' she said, 'only in your greatest need, and I will come.' Zal came down the mountain carrying a feather that was also a promise — and the Shahnameh's greatest hero was now one generation closer to being born.
chapters.summary_fa: سام پسرش را که با موهایِ سفید متولد شده بود در البرز رها کرد. سیمرغ او را برداشت و در آشیانه‌اش پرورش داد. سام خواب دید و برگشت. سیمرغ زال را با یک پر و یک وعده بازگرداند.
chapters.summary_tg: Сом писарашро дар Алборз гузошт. Симурғ бардошт ва дар лона калон кард. Сом рӯъё дид ва баргашт. Симурғ Золро бо пар ва ваъда баргардонд.

chapters.title: Rudabeh — The Tower of Hair
chapters.summary: A princess lets her hair down from the tower. Love enters the chronicle before war — and Rostam's father is won.
chapters.story:
Zal came down from the mountain changed. He had lived with the Simorgh; he had the long patience of a creature raised by something older than kingship. When merchants described Rudabeh — princess of Kabul, daughter of Mehrab, her face like the moon and her hair a river of silk — Zal fell in love through words alone, before he had seen her face. This is how the Shahnameh treats love: not as accident but as recognition. Rudabeh heard of him in the same season from her handmaidens, who had seen him at the market, and she fell in love before she had seen his face either. Two people falling in love through description, across a distance — the chronicle finds this more reliable than love at first sight.

The handmaidens arranged a meeting in the garden below Rudabeh's tower. Rudabeh let her hair down from the window — hair so long it reached the ground — and Zal climbed up. They spent the night in her chamber pledging their lives while the city of Kabul slept beneath them. The obstacles the morning brought were serious. Sam refused: Rudabeh's line traced back to Zahhak. Manuchehr the king refused: the same reason. Sindokht, Rudabeh's mother, negotiated with the ferocity of a general. Astrologers were consulted, as they are consulted when the powerful want the stars to confirm what they have already decided. The stars agreed: from this union would come a child unlike any other. Permission was granted.

Zal and Rudabeh were married. Nine months later, the child would not come. Rudabeh was dying. Zal burned the Simorgh's feather. The great bird came, guided the caesarean that Sam's surgeons performed, and breathed healing over Rudabeh as the child was lifted free. The child was large as a young lion and roared like one. They named him Rostam.
chapters.summary_fa: زال از طریقِ توصیف عاشق رودابه شد. رودابه هم از طریقِ توصیف عاشقِ زال شد. ندیمه‌ها ملاقاتی در باغ ترتیب دادند. رودابه موهایش را از پنجره آویخت. زال بالا رفت.
chapters.summary_tg: Зол аз тавсиф ба Рӯдоба ошиқ шуд. Рӯдоба ҳам. Надима вохӯриро дар боғ тартиб дод. Рӯдоба мӯяшро овезон кард. Зол боло рафт.

chapters.title: Birth of Rostam
chapters.summary: Zal burns the Simorgh's feather. Through pain and fire, the greatest pahlavan enters the world.
chapters.story:
Nine months after the wedding the birth would not come. Rudabeh grew weak; the court's physicians stood at her bed and found themselves useless. Zal understood what kind of moment this was. He took the Simorgh's feather from the cloth where he had kept it since the day he descended from Alborz — through every battle, every court, every year — and he burned it. The smoke rose. The Simorgh came. She guided the caesarean that Sam's surgeons performed, and breathed over Rudabeh as the child was lifted free. Rudabeh lived. The feather was gone.

The child was large as a young lion, and loud as one. He needed ten wet nurses the first week because no one of them had enough. By the time he was a year old he ate meat. By the time he was seven his frame was a grown man's frame, and the court had quietly stopped treating him as a child. At twelve he walked along the horse lines in Zabulestan pressing each candidate's back, testing strength. Three thousand horses buckled. At the end of the line one did not move — a spotted horse, Rakhsh, chosen.

The first formal test came when a rogue war elephant broke loose and ran through the palace. Guards fled. Zal's court cleared. Rostam, twelve years old, took a mace from the wall, walked into the corridor, and struck once. The elephant fell and did not rise. The mace was bent. The corridor was silent in a way that meant something new had just been established — a pillar the world would lean against for the next five generations of kings.
chapters.summary_fa: زال پرِ سیمرغ را سوزاند. سیمرغ سزارینی را که سامِ جراحان انجام دادند راهنمایی کرد. رودابه زندگی. فرزند مثلِ شیرِ جوان بزرگ بود و مثلِ او بانگ برآورد. نامش را رستم گذاشتند.
chapters.summary_tg: Зол пари Симурғро сӯзонд. Симурғ омад. Рӯдоба зиндагӣ. Фарзанд монанди шерча буд. Номашро Рустам гузоштанд.

chapters.title: Rostam — Pahlavan of the Age
chapters.summary: Seven labours, one Rakhsh, no equal under the sky. Rostam becomes the world's pillar of arms.
chapters.story:
Rostam pressed ten thousand horses on the plains of Zabulestan. Ten thousand buckled under his hand. Rakhsh held. He was spotted and fierce and he chose his rider as decisively as his rider chose him. From that moment they were inseparable — not rider and mount but two halves of a single force that the Shahnameh would need for longer than any kingdom lasts.

The Seven Labours came first: a lion killed by Rakhsh while Rostam slept; a desert crossed by divine mercy; a dragon defeated by learning to trust the loyal; a sorceress unmasked by a name of God; a warden captured and converted into a guide; a demon general beheaded at the gates of Mazandaran; and finally Div-e Sepid — the White Demon — whose liver-blood dripped into blind eyes and gave back sight to Kay Kavus and all of Iran's captive warriors. Seven trials, seven lessons. The chronicle does not present them as victories so much as educations.

But Rostam's story does not end with the Seven Labours — it has barely begun. He serves five kings across centuries, each more reckless than the last. He rescues Kay Kavus from Mazandaran, from the sky, from his own pride, more than once. He fights Akvan the Div, who grants wishes by destroying them. He wrestles Afrasiab's forces at the Oxus for decades. He meets his own son Sohrab on the battlefield without knowing it — and kills him. He meets Esfandiyar, the righteous man his equal in strength, and is forced to destroy him too. Each killing is heavier than the one before. Ferdowsi uses Rostam to ask a question the Shahnameh never answers directly: what does it cost to be the one who holds the world together when the world will not hold itself?
chapters.summary_fa: رستم ده هزار اسب را فشرد. رخش ایستاد. هفت خان آمد — شیری که رخش کشت، بیابان، اژدها، جادوگری، نگهبانی، سردارِ دیوان، دیوِ سپید. هر آزمون درسی بود. هفت خان هرگز تمام نمی‌شود.
chapters.summary_tg: Рустам даҳ ҳазор асп фишурд. Рахш истод. Ҳафтхон омад. Ҳар озмун дарсе буд. Ҳафтхон тамом намешавад.

chapters.title: Sohrab — Son of the Storm
chapters.summary: Two armies camp on opposite shores. Father and son, unknowing, raise blades against each other.
chapters.story:
Rostam spent one night at Samangan between missions. Tahmineh, the princess, came to his chamber in the dark — not from weakness but from purpose. She had heard of him for years and wanted a son from him. She told him this directly. He gave her his arm bracelet before he left: 'If a daughter, put it in her hair. If a son, bind it to his arm.' He left before morning. Sohrab was born and grew at three times the normal rate. When he was twelve he asked his mother who his father was. She told him. He decided on the spot: he would find Rostam, and together they would overthrow Kay Kavus and Afrasiab and rule father-and-son. He was twelve and he meant every word. He led the Turanian army toward Iran.

The armies met at the White Castle. Sohrab challenged the Iranian champion to single combat. Rostam came out in disguise — he had heard of this terrifying young warrior and chose not to reveal who he was. They fought. The first day Sohrab pinned Rostam to the ground and asked his name. Rostam lied. Sohrab let him live — there was something in the old man he recognized without being able to name. The second day Rostam drove his sword into Sohrab's side.

Sohrab spoke from the ground: 'My father Rostam will find you and destroy you.' Rostam's heart understood before his mind did. He asked to see the arm. The bracelet was there. He had killed his son.

Kay Kavus kept a medicine that could save any wound. Rostam begged for it on his knees. Kay Kavus refused: a warrior as powerful as Sohrab, healed, would unbalance the kingdom's politics. The medicine was not sent. Sohrab died as the sun set, his head in his father's arms, between the two armies. The Shahnameh does not soften this. It records it exactly as it happened and then continues — because the chronicle has never stopped for grief before, and it will not stop now.
chapters.summary_fa: رستم یک شب در سمنگان ماند. تهمینه آمد. بازوبند را داد. سهراب متولد شد، با سه برابرِ سرعتِ معمول رشد کرد، دوازده‌ساله فهمید پدرش کیست. در دشت روبرو شدند. رستم پسرش را کشت.
chapters.summary_tg: Рустам як шаб дар Самангон монд. Таҳмина омад. Браслетро дод. Суҳроб таваллуд шуд, калон шуд, медонист. Дар майдон рӯ ба рӯ шуданд. Рустам писарашро кушт.

chapters.title: Siavash — The Pure Prince
chapters.summary: A prince too pure for a corrupt court walks through fire to prove his innocence. He will not return.
chapters.story:
Siavash was raised by Rostam and came back to Kay Kavus's court as a young man who had been trained by the most rigorous standard of honour in Iran. His stepmother Sudabeh wanted him. He refused. She accused him of assault. Kay Kavus, unable to resolve the contradiction, decreed trial by fire. Seven mountains of fire were built. Siavash rode through all seven on horseback and emerged unmarked. His innocence was proven absolutely. The court was still corrupt.

Siavash led Iran's army against Afrasiab and negotiated an honest peace. Kay Kavus refused to ratify it and ordered the war to continue. Siavash read the orders and understood: there was no version of this court that would let him be right. He wrote a letter to his father explaining his reasoning and crossed the Oxus into Turan. He asked Afrasiab for asylum. Afrasiab, who had dreamed of him — a young man on a white horse, his greatest joy and his coming destruction — accepted. He gave Siavash his daughter Farangis and land. Siavash built a city called Siyavashgerd — City of Siavash — and ruled it justly. For a few years he was, improbably, happy.

Afrasiab's general Garsivaz hated Siavash for what Siavash made him look like by comparison. He began the slow work of poisoning: a question here, a doubt planted there, a suspicion watered until it bloomed. He told Afrasiab that the city was a fortress, that the letters to the border were treasonous, that the foreign prince was planning to use Turan against itself. Afrasiab, old and afraid of his own dreams, believed him. He ordered Siavash's arrest.

When the soldiers came, Siavash did not fight them. He was taken to a field outside his own city and beheaded. Where his blood fell on the earth, a plant grew immediately — not slowly but at once, as though the earth had been waiting. Ferdowsi calls it the blood of Siavash. Farangis, pregnant with Kay Khosrow, fled east. The people of Iran mourned Siavash every year at the ceremony of his tears. He had done nothing wrong. He had been purer than the chronicle he was born into, and the chronicle had destroyed him for it.
chapters.summary_fa: سیاوش از هفت کوهِ آتش سوار عبور کرد و دست‌نخورده. بی‌گناهیش ثابت شد اما دربار خیلی فاسد بود. از جیحون گذشت. در توران شهر ساخت. گرسیوز ذهنِ افراسیاب را مسموم کرد. سر بریده شد. خونش گیاه شد.
chapters.summary_tg: Сиёвуш аз ҳафт куҳи оташ гузашт. Беноҳиаш исбот шуд аммо дарбор фосид буд. Аз Ҷайҳун гузашт. Дар Турон шаҳр сохт. Гарсевоз заҳролуд кард. Сар бурида шуд.

chapters.title: Kay Kavus — The Reckless King
chapters.summary: A king who challenges the sky and loses. Rostam must rescue him — again and again.
chapters.story:
A demon came to Kay Kavus's court disguised as a musician. He was gifted, his voice was beautiful, and he sang about Mazandaran — a land of riches, no king to resist Iran, forests full of prey. He sang it as a place a great king would claim if only he had the ambition. Kay Kavus had the ambition. Zal, Sam, and Rostam all said the same thing: do not go. The warnings made him more eager. He marched. The demon, resuming its true shape, rode at the head of the Iranian army to show the way.

Mazandaran was everything the warnings had described. The White Demon — Div-e Sepid, greatest of the Mazandaran demons — led a counterattack at night. He did not kill the army; he blinded it. By dawn Kay Kavus and every soldier sat sightless in a foreign land. Living blind in enemy territory is a more precise punishment than death. Rostam was summoned. The Seven Labours began — seven obstacles between the Iranian camp and Div-e Sepid's fortress, each requiring a different kind of courage. None of them stopped Rostam. He tore out Div-e Sepid's liver, brought the blood back, and dropped three drops into each blinded eye. Sight returned. Kay Kavus thanked Rostam in the language kings use to thank those who save them from their own mistakes, which does not include acknowledging the mistake.

Later, Kay Kavus built a machine. The principle was simple: a throne on a frame, a trained eagle at each corner, a piece of meat held above each eagle on a rod just out of their reach. The eagles fly upward toward the meat; the throne rises with them. He rode it into the sky, above the clouds, above everything. Then the eagles tired. The throne fell. It hit the earth somewhere in China. Kay Kavus lay in the wreckage, unhurt because the chronicle was not yet finished with him, and waited. Rostam was dispatched again.

And there was the matter of Sohrab's medicine — the cure that heals any wound, which Kay Kavus possessed. Rostam came on his knees, begging, for the first and only time in the chronicle. Kay Kavus performed his calculation: a warrior as powerful as Sohrab, healed, would unbalance the kingdom. He refused. Sohrab died. The Shahnameh records all of this with patient precision and asks, chapter after chapter: what does it cost to serve a king who confuses boldness with wisdom?
chapters.summary_fa: دیوی به شکلِ موسیقیدان از مازندران خواند. کی‌کاووس باوجودِ همه‌ی هشدارها رفت. سپاه کور شد. رستم هفت خان را طی کرد و بازشان گرداند. بعد کی‌کاووس به آسمان پرواز کرد — و افتاد. رستم دوباره آمد.
chapters.summary_tg: Дев ба шакли созанда аз Мозандарон хонд. Кай Кову рафт. Сипоҳ кӯр шуд. Рустам Ҳафтхонро гузашт. Баъд Кай Кову ба осмон парвоз кард — ва афтод.

chapters.title: Kay Khosrow — The Chosen King
chapters.summary: Son of the martyred Siavash, Kay Khosrow is destiny's chosen king. His reign is the chronicle's golden age.
chapters.story:
Farangis gave birth in the Turanian wilderness and raised her son in hiding. She told him who his father was. She told him what had been done to his father. Kay Khosrow grew up tending herds in the land of his father's killers, knowing exactly who he was, giving no outward sign of it. Patience here was not weakness — it was the quality the situation demanded. Giv, one of Iran's great paladins, spent seven years searching for him in Turan. When he finally found a shepherd boy on an open hillside, there was no mistaking what he had found.

Rostam came across the Oxus to bring them home. The succession question in Kay Kavus's court was not obvious: Fariborz was the elder son, familiar, with supporters. The test was set: both princes would attempt to open the gates of a great fortress. Fariborz led a full military assault. He failed. Kay Khosrow arrived at the gate alone, prayed, and the gate opened. The Shahnameh records this without commentary. No army. No battering ram. The gate opened because Kay Khosrow asked it to, and that was that.

He organized the great war against Afrasiab — not from ambition but from debt. Siavash's blood was in Turanian earth. Campaign by campaign, the Iranian army reduced Turan's power. Afrasiab fled north, west, east, was cornered and escaped, again and again. At the edge of a remote lake, Kay Khosrow finally found him. He made the execution personal, with his own hands, because the debt was personal. Afrasiab died. The Iran-Turan wars that had shaped the chronicle for centuries closed.

He reigned justly for years at the golden height of the Kayanian dynasty. Then, at his zenith, he announced he was leaving. He had seen what the throne does to those who sit on it too long. He named Kay Kavus. He said: I will not wait. He distributed the kingdom, said his farewells, and walked into the Alborz mountains with a handful of paladins. A snowstorm rose. When it passed, he was gone. The Shahnameh does not say where he went. It says only that he was not seen again — and that he was the only king in the chronicle who walked out of his reign freely, at the height of his power, before corruption could find him.
chapters.summary_fa: کی‌خسرو در توران به عنوانِ چوپان‌زاده رشد کرد. گیو هفت سال دنبالش گشت. جنگِ بزرگ برای انتقامِ سیاوش. افراسیاب کنارِ دریاچه اعدام شد. بعد کی‌خسرو انتخاب کرد که برود — به کوه رفت و دیده نشد.
chapters.summary_tg: Кай Хусрав дар Турон чӯпонзода калон шуд. Гев ҳафт сол ҷустуҷӯ кард. Ҷанги бузург. Афросиёб кнари дарёча иҷро шуд. Баъд Кай Хусрав рафт — ба кӯҳ рафт ва дида нашуд.

chapters.title: Akvan Div — The Demon of the Lake
chapters.summary: A demon that grants wishes by twisting them. Rostam is hurled into the sea — and emerges unconquered.
chapters.story:
Something was moving through the Iranian border herds killing systematically — dozens of animals left where they fell, not eaten. The herdsmen described a wild horse of impossible speed. Kay Khosrow made the assignment simple: Rostam. Rostam went with Rakhsh and his hunting lasso and the confidence of a man who has not been stopped by anything yet. He tracked the creature for five days before he was close enough to throw the lasso. It caught — he felt the weight of something substantial on the rope — and then it was gone. The rope was intact. Nothing on it. Rostam coiled the lasso back and understood: a horse does not do that. A demon does.

He made camp and went to sleep. The Shahnameh records this without comment. He was tired from five days of chase. The same quality that makes him the champion of the world made him capable of this particular error — he has never been caught, so he has no model for being caught. Akvan came while he slept. Rather than attack directly, the demon dug up a square of earth with Rostam sleeping on it and carried him into the sky. Rostam woke above the clouds, lying on a piece of borderland, looking down at nothing.

Akvan offered the choice with a demon's formal pleasure: shall I throw you onto the mountain, where you'll break on the rocks, or into the sea, where you'll drown? Rostam was awake now. He had the dissolving lasso as his evidence, and from it he had derived Akvan's nature: a div who inverts — who grants wishes by giving the opposite of what you ask. The logic ran one way: ask for the mountain, receive the sea. He knew which of those he could survive. He asked for the mountain. Akvan threw him into the sea.

Rostam hit the water at great speed, went deep, and swam. He climbed out at the shore and Rakhsh was there — the horse had followed the sound to the water's edge and waited. Rostam found Akvan, fought through the demon's illusions by not relying on what he could see, found the real centre of the thing, and struck. Akvan Div died on the Iranian borderland. The herds were safe. Rostam went back. The Shahnameh moved on — this chapter was always about cleverness, and the cleverness had been demonstrated.
chapters.summary_fa: اکوان دیو در شکلِ اسبِ وحشی گله‌ها را ویران می‌کرد. رستم کمند انداخت — کمند حل شد. رستم خوابید. اکوان بلندش کرد. کوه یا دریا؟ رستم منطقِ وارونه را فهمید. کوه را خواست. به دریا انداخته شد. زنده ماند.
chapters.summary_tg: Аквон дев ба шакли асп рамаҳоро хароб мекард. Рустам камандашро андохт — ҳал шуд. Аквон бардошт. Куҳ ё дарё? Рустам фаҳмид. Кӯҳро хост. Дарё афтод.

chapters.title: Bijan and Manijeh — Pit and Rose
chapters.title_fa: بیژن و منیژه — چاه و گل
chapters.summary: A warrior falls into a pit for love. A princess bribes the world to free him. A rescue across three winters.
chapters.story:
Bijan and Gorgin were sent to the Armenian border to deal with wild boars. They dealt with the boars. On the way back, Gorgin described something: a Turanian spring festival nearby, Manijeh, daughter of Afrasiab, celebrating with her attendants, barely any guards. The description was designed to work. Bijan put on his finest clothes and crossed the border.

Manijeh saw him at the festival and decided immediately. She had him drugged and brought to her chambers in Afrasiab's palace. When he woke, he was in a room he had not chosen, in a kingdom technically at war with his own. When Afrasiab's guards found him, the king made two rapid decisions: Bijan into a pit — a deep stone well sealed with a boulder so heavy it could not be lifted by ordinary means — and Manijeh expelled from the palace. She was his daughter; he did not execute her. He stripped her of everything else and sent her out the gates.

Manijeh went to the market. She begged bread. She took it to the edge of the pit and found the crack in the boulder's seal and pushed food through. She did this the next day. And the next. The Shahnameh measures the passage of time in winters: one, then two, then three. The boulder sat. Bijan was alive inside it. Manijeh was outside it every day.

In Iran, Kay Khosrow brought out the Jame-e-Jam — the world-showing cup — and saw Bijan alive in a pit in Turan. He chose Rostam for the mission, because whoever had sealed the pit had done so knowing only Rostam could open it. Rostam crossed the border disguised as a merchant with a caravan and Rakhsh in the horse lines.

Manijeh had been watching every caravan for three years. She walked Rostam's horse lines at dusk and saw Rakhsh. She knew. She led him to the pit that night. Rostam gripped the boulder. It was not a normal boulder. Then it moved. He tossed it aside and lowered a rope. Bijan climbed out — bone-thin, worn by three years of darkness, alive. They fought their way back to Iran. Manijeh crossed with them. She had kept him alive through three winters by her own means, and the Shahnameh brings her to Iran because she earned the crossing.
chapters.summary_fa: بیژن با تشویقِ گرگین به جشنِ بهارِ توران رفت. منیژه دیدش و مسموم کرد. چاه. سه زمستانِ گدایی. کی‌خسرو جامِ جهان‌نما را دید. رستم به عنوانِ بازرگان رفت. منیژه رخش را پیدا کرد. سنگ برداشته شد.
chapters.summary_tg: Беҷан ба ҷашни баҳор рафт. Манижа дид ва захролуд кард. Чоҳ. Се зимистони гадоӣ. Рустам ҳамчун тоҷир рафт. Манижа Рахшро ёфт. Санг бардошта шуд.

chapters.title: The Great War — Iran and Turan
chapters.summary: The final war between Iran and Turan. Kay Khosrow crosses the Oxus. A thousand years of enmity closes.
chapters.story:
Kay Khosrow organized the war with the patience of a man who had spent his childhood in the land he was now invading. He named the commanders: Tus led the vanguard, Gudarz the center, Rostam the decisive force. The Derafsh Kaviani moved east across the Oxus. Every soldier knew why they were crossing. This was not Kay Kavus's reckless invasion of Mazandaran. This was a war of debt — Siavash's blood, Siyavashgerd, the mourning plant that still grew in Turanian soil.

The war's first wound was self-inflicted. Kay Khosrow had a half-brother named Frud — Siavash's son by a Turanian mother, loyal to Iran, living in a castle on the march. The king had sent specific instructions to Tus: do not approach Frud's territory. Tus ignored the order. Frud was killed. The war organized to avenge Siavash killed Siavash's own son in its opening days.

Turan's resistance was organized by Piran Wiseh — the general who had tried hardest to save Siavash, who had failed, and who now served Afrasiab's cause faithfully despite knowing what it had cost. He was the most capable military mind in Turan. After years of grinding battle, both armies agreed to settle part of the war by a contest of twelve champions each. Iran won. Then Gudarz and Piran met in single combat — two old generals who respected each other and could not stop. Piran fell. The Turanian army lost its organizing intelligence. It did not collapse immediately, but the quality was gone from it.

Afrasiab retreated north, west, east. He had ruled Turan for a century and he ran with the exhausted cunning of a king who has outlived his justification. Kay Khosrow followed with the patience of someone raised in this landscape, in no hurry because there was no longer anywhere to go. At the edge of a remote lake, he found him. The execution was personal — this was his father's blood. Afrasiab died at the lake. The Iran-Turan wars that had shaped the Shahnameh since the Nozar chapter — the wars that had killed Siavash, consumed Piran Wiseh, and cost three generations of Iranian paladins — closed at the lake without ceremony.
chapters.summary_fa: کی‌خسرو جنگِ بزرگ را برای بدهیِ سیاوش سازماندهی کرد. طوس فرود را کشت — اولین زخمِ جنگ. گودرز و پیرانِ ویسه آخرین بار روبرو شدند. پیران افتاد. افراسیاب کنارِ دریاچه یافته شد و اعدام شد.
chapters.summary_tg: Кай Хусрав ҷанги бузургро ташкил кард. Тус Фарудро кушт. Гударз ва Пирони Виса охирин бор рӯ ба рӯ шуданд. Пиран афтод. Афросиёб дарёча иҷро шуд.

chapters.title: Lohrasp — The Humble King
chapters.summary: Kay Khosrow vanishes into the mountain and passes the crown to Lohrasp — a transfer that surprises a kingdom.
chapters.story:
When Kay Khosrow announced Lohrasp as his successor, the court's unhappiness was not petty. The paladins who had won the great war — Tus, Fariborz, Gudarz's family — had reasonable expectations. They had fought for decades. The successor should come from among them. Lohrasp was a court official with no great battle to his name. Kay Khosrow's response was not a defense of Lohrasp's military record. He said: the kingdom has just finished the most destructive war in its history. A king formed by war governs in war's idiom. What is needed now is the man who can govern in peace's idiom.

Lohrasp ruled for decades and the Shahnameh gives his reign little space — which is the chronicle's compliment. There is nothing dramatic to report. The borders held. The disputes were settled. He administered with the attention of a man who understood that administration is what kingdoms are actually for. He did not invade demon-territory or fly to the sky or refuse medicine to dying sons. The absence of catastrophe is the evidence of competence.

His son Goshtasp had the kind of sensitivity to slight that occasionally tips into crisis. He felt dishonored by some incident at court — the Shahnameh does not elaborate — and fled abroad. He made his way to the Roman empire, worked in disguise, won a contest, and married Ketayun, daughter of the emperor. He returned with achievement and ambition. Lohrasp looked at his son and gave him the throne cleanly, without negotiation, recognizing that what Goshtasp had needed all along was not his father's defeat but his father's confidence.

Lohrasp retired to the fire temple of Balkh to live as a worshipper. When Arjasp's Hephthalite invasion reached the city, the old king was offered escape. He refused. He died defending the fire. The Shahnameh does not call this tragedy. It uses the word for a man who died exactly as he had lived: holding something worth holding.
chapters.summary_fa: کی‌خسرو تاج را به لهراسپ سپرد — نه طوس، نه فریبرز. دربار ناراضی بود. لهراسپ دهه‌ها بدونِ درامِ بزرگی اداره کرد. پسرش گشتاسپ فرار کرد و برگشت. لهراسپ تخت را داد. در آتشکده‌ی بلخ مُرد.
chapters.summary_tg: Кай Хусрав тоҷро ба Луҳросп дод. Дарбор норозӣ буд. Луҳросп даҳсолаҳо идора кард. Писараш Гуштосп гурехт ва баргашт. Луҳросп тахтро дод. Дар оташкадаи Балх мурд.

chapters.title: Goshtasp and Zoroaster
chapters.summary: Zoroaster comes to the court of Goshtasp. Fire temples are lit. A new faith is threaded into the old chronicle.
chapters.story:
Goshtasp had inherited the throne from Lohrasp and ruled with the particular energy of a man who had made himself in foreign lands. Then Zoroaster arrived at his court from the east — from the region of Rai — carrying the Avesta and the testimony of a direct encounter with Ahura Mazda. The court received him with the standard skepticism of courts. There were contests of wisdom, questions from the Magi, challenges from scholars who had served the old fires. Zoroaster answered each question with the precision of a man reporting conviction rather than performing it. Goshtasp converted not from amazement but from recognition: this message was true in the specific way that changes what you do next.

He organized the faith into the kingdom's structure. Fire temples were established across Iran. The Avesta was distributed. Esfandiyar — his eldest son, the greatest warrior of his age — was sent to bring the Good Religion to the unconverted kingdoms. The mission was genuine: Esfandiyar believed. It was also politically convenient: a righteous son on a holy mission is not at court competing for the throne.

Arjasp, king of the Hephthalites, refused. He invaded with Hephthalite forces and killed Lohrasp at the fire temple of Balkh, extinguishing the sacred fire. He captured Goshtasp's daughters. Goshtasp called Esfandiyar back from his missions and gave him the assignment: defeat Arjasp, rescue the daughters, restore the fire. He promised the throne on completion. Esfandiyar went. He succeeded. The throne was not given. Jamasp the astrologer warned Goshtasp that a son with Esfandiyar's power and popularity was a structural threat to any sitting king. Goshtasp heard the warning and found it convenient. He promised a new mission instead. Esfandiyar obeyed. The Shahnameh records this cycle with quiet precision: a father who fears his son's greatness, and a son too righteous to refuse his father's commands, moving in circles that are slowly tightening toward an outcome neither of them can stop.
chapters.summary_fa: زرتشت به دربارِ گشتاسپ رسید. پیامِ اهورا مزدا را آورد. گشتاسپ تبدیل شد. آتشکده‌ها روشن شدند. اسفندیار برای گسترشِ دین فرستاده شد. ارجاسپ رفض کرد و حمله کرد. دایره‌ای که دارد تنگ می‌شود شروع شد.
chapters.summary_tg: Зардушт ба дарбори Гуштосп расид. Паёми Аҳура Мазда овард. Гуштосп табдил шуд. Оташкадаҳо равшан шуданд. Исфандиёр фиристода шуд. Арҷосп рад кард ва ҳамла кард.

chapters.title: Esfandiyar — The Brazen-Bodied
chapters.summary: Steel cannot cut him, except where his eyes can be reached.
chapters.story:
In his youth, Zoroaster bathed Esfandiyar in sacred water and his body became brazen — no iron could pierce his skin. His eyes were open at the moment of immersion. That is the one place iron can reach him. He grew up knowing this as a fact about himself the way a man knows his own height.

He served Goshtasp for decades with no treachery in him. He defeated Arjasp, converted kingdoms, rescued captives, restored sacred fires. Each time he returned expecting the throne that had been promised. Each time a new task was invented. When a courtier named Gurz-Ahmar provided false testimony against him, Goshtasp had him imprisoned at the remote fortress of Gumbadan without trial. Esfandiyar did not plot escape. He did not organize his supporters. He waited. Arjasp invaded again; Goshtasp needed him and released him.

Esfandiyar went back to war. He completed his Seven Labours on the road to Arjasp's stronghold — wolves, lions, a dragon, a sorceress, a great bird, the killing cold, and finally the Brazen Fortress itself, which he entered disguised as a merchant and destroyed from within. He rescued his sisters. He returned with the victory his father had demanded.

Goshtasp's final command was specific: bring Rostam of Zabulestan to court in chains. Jamasp the astrologer told Esfandiyar plainly: this mission will kill you. Esfandiyar replied that he knew. He went anyway. He was too righteous to disobey his father's command, too honest to pretend he had a reason not to go, too courageous to let the knowledge of his own death stop him. The Shahnameh builds his biography as the structure of an inevitable tragedy: a man too good for the world it depicts, who will be broken by it for exactly that reason.
chapters.summary_fa: زرتشت اسفندیار را در آبِ مقدس غسل داد و رویین‌تن شد — جز در چشمانش. دهه‌ها بدونِ هیچ خیانتی خدمت کرد. یک بار زندانی شد. در نهایت فرمان آمد: رستم را با زنجیر بیاور. دانست خواهد کشت. رفت.
chapters.summary_tg: Зардушт Исфандиёрро дар оби муқаддас ғусл дод ва рӯин шуд — ҷуз чашмонаш. Даҳсолаҳо бе хиёнат хидмат кард. Фармон омад. Медонист мекушад. Рафт.

chapters.title: Esfandiyar's Seven Labours
chapters.summary: Before facing Rostam, Esfandiyar's seven tests begin. Each labour is a world in itself.
chapters.story:
Arjasp held Goshtasp's daughters in the Brazen Fortress at the edge of the Hephthalite kingdom, and the road to the fortress ran through seven stations of increasing difficulty.

The first two were wolves and then lions — creatures of the natural world amplified to the supernatural scale the Haft Khan requires. Esfandiyar killed them from horseback and noted that strength against strength was the test he was least likely to fail. The harder trials would follow.

The third was a dragon. Esfandiyar built a device of spiked wheels on his chariot and drove into the dragon's mouth. The spikes did what arrows could not. The fourth was a sorceress who appeared as a beautiful young woman, offering rest after three stations of violence. Esfandiyar spoke the name of Ahura Mazda. The false form dissolved. The fifth was a great bird that dove with the force of a storm. Esfandiyar let it strike his brazen body, took the full impact without damage, and killed it when it could not recover from its own strike. The sixth was a region of killing cold — three days of frost and white expanse. He walked through without stopping.

The seventh station was the fortress itself. It could not be taken by force. Esfandiyar arrived at the gates as a merchant with goods to sell. He was admitted, moved through the fortress for two days mapping its structure, then acted on the third: killed Arjasp's key commanders, freed his sisters Homay and Beh-Afarid, and burned the fortress from inside. The seven labours established his claim to stand beside Rostam — the only other figure in the chronicle who had completed such a sequence. They were also completed in service of a father who would then imprison him, deny him the throne, and eventually send him to die.
chapters.summary_fa: ارجاسپ دختراتِ گشتاسپ را در دژِ روئین نگه می‌داشت. اسفندیار هفت آزمون را طی کرد: گرگان، شیران، اژدها (ارابه‌ی تیز)، جادوگر (نامِ اهورا مزدا)، پرنده‌ی بزرگ، سرما، و دژِ روئین با تغییرِ قیافه.
chapters.summary_tg: Арҷосп духтарони Гуштоспро дар Деҷи Руин нигоҳ дошт. Исфандиёр ҳафт озмонро тай кард: гургон, шерон, аждаҳо, ҷодугар, паррандаи бузург, сармо, деж.

chapters.title: The Great Clash
chapters.summary: Two pahlavans who cannot both live. One by duty, one by pride. The Simorgh's feather decides everything.
chapters.story:
Esfandiyar arrived at Zabulestan carrying Goshtasp's command: bring Rostam to court in chains. Rostam received him as a guest — feasts, ceremony, the full hospitality of Zabulestan. He knew who Esfandiyar was. He proposed every alternative: travel to court freely, swear any oath before any fire, acknowledge the king's authority in any form except being bound. Esfandiyar heard every argument and agreed with most of them. The king's command was specific. He had no authority to change it.

They fought on the plain. The first day established the problem precisely: Rostam's arrows hit Esfandiyar's brazen body and left no mark. Esfandiyar's weapons cut Rostam — the first time in the chronicle that Rostam has bled in single combat from a human opponent. The second day was the first at greater intensity. By its end Rostam was wounded in multiple places, Rakhsh was weakened, and the situation was clear. He asked Esfandiyar to hold until morning. Esfandiyar agreed, because he had already won and could not press the advantage against someone he respected.

Zal burned the Simorgh's feather — the same promise carried since Alborz. The Simorgh came. She healed them both and grieved, because she was the world's oldest witness and she knew what was about to happen and had no way to prevent it. She told Rostam: the tamarisk tree by the river. Two-pronged arrow. Aim for the eyes. Rostam said he would be cursed for it. The Simorgh said he would be. She departed.

Rostam made the arrow himself. He came back on the third day and they fought again. The arrow found Esfandiyar's eyes. He fell. Dying, he told Rostam: you are not the cause of my death. The man who sent me here knowing what it would produce — that is the cause. His name is Goshtasp. My father. Jamasp cursed Rostam. Rostam accepted the curse without argument. The Shahnameh pauses here longer than it has paused for any death since Sohrab.
chapters.summary_fa: اسفندیار با فرمانِ پدرش رسید: رستم را با زنجیر بیاور. دو روز جنگیدند. تیرهایِ رستم در رویین‌تن نگرفتند. رستم زخمی شد. سیمرغ آمد و گفت: تیرِ گز. چشمان. رستم رفت. تیر پیدا کرد. اسفندیار آخرین کلماتش پدرش را سرزنش کرد.
chapters.summary_tg: Исфандиёр бо фармони падараш расид. Ду рӯз ҷангиданд. Тирҳои Рустам дар рӯин нагирифтанд. Симурғ омад: тири газ. Чашмон. Рустам рафт. Тир ёфт. Исфандиёр охирин суханон падарашро сарзаниш кард.

chapters.title: Simorgh — The Phoenix Council
chapters.summary: Wings the colour of the sun. The mountain remembers a wisdom older than language.
chapters.story:
The Simorgh is not a bird. She has the form of a bird — vast wings, feathers the colour of the sun and the deepest fires, a size that makes the mountain seem small — but the Shahnameh does not describe her as a creature of the natural world. She nests on the world-tree Vourukasha on Alborz and has watched three cycles of the world's destruction and renewal. She is, in the most precise sense, the world's own memory.

She appears four times in the chronicle with decisive effect. She raised Zal on the mountain when Sam abandoned him, educated him with the patience of something that has watched everything, and returned him to his father with a feather and a promise. She guided the caesarean that saved Rudabeh and produced Rostam, when Zal burned the feather for the first time. She healed Rostam and armed him for the clash with Esfandiyar, when Zal burned the feather for the last time — and she grieved, because she knew what she was enabling and had no way to prevent the cost of it.

Each intervention enables the story to continue but does not make the story cost less. She is not a savior. She is the mechanism that keeps the chronicle moving when it would otherwise stop. She told Rostam he would be cursed for killing Esfandiyar. He would be. She provided the means anyway, because the alternative was the story stopping.

The Shahnameh says she was not seen again after leaving Rostam on the eve of the clash. She does not die — she is older than death. She does not announce a permanent departure. She goes, and does not return. The line of Zal's great stories — the Seven Labours, Sohrab, Esfandiyar — are ending. The feather is ash. The promise has been kept. The oldest witness returns to her mountain, and the chronicle continues without her.
chapters.summary_fa: سیمرغ در درختِ جهانی در البرز لانه دارد و سه نابودیِ دنیا را تماشا کرده. چهار بار تاریخ را تغییر داد: پرورشِ زال، تولدِ رستم، مسلح کردنِ رستم در برابرِ اسفندیار. هر بار غم می‌خورد. هر بار کمک می‌کند.
chapters.summary_tg: Симурғ дар дарахти ҷаҳонӣ дар Алборз лона дорад. Чаҳор бор таърихро тағйир дод: Зол, Рустам, Исфандиёр. Ҳар бор ғам мехӯрад. Ҳар бор кӯмак мекунад.

chapters.title: Rostam's Last Stand
chapters.summary: A half-brother's treachery. A pit of iron stakes. The world's pillar of arms falls — and the chronicle goes quiet.

chapters.title: Bahman — Avenger's Son
chapters.summary: Esfandiyar's son rules with grief and ambition. The Kayanian house turns on itself.

chapters.title: Homay — The Warrior Queen
chapters.summary: A queen, not a king, takes the throne — and proves sharper than the swords around her.

chapters.title: Darab — The Foundling Prince
chapters.summary: Abandoned in a chest on the river, raised by a launderer, Darab reclaims a kingdom that forgot him.

chapters.title: Dara — The Last Achaemenid
chapters.summary: The last Achaemenid. Pride before the Greek tide. A king who would not bend, and so is broken.

chapters.title: Alexander — The Two-Horned
chapters.summary: Ferdowsi's Alexander carries both philosophy and a sword. He is Iranian by a twist of blood — and the world bows.

chapters.title: The Ashkanian Age
chapters.summary: The Arsacids rule in fragments. Many small kings, many small wars. The chronicle dims between golden ages.

chapters.title: Ardavan — The Last Arsacid
chapters.summary: The last Parthian king sees a new fire rising from Pars. He fights it — and the old age ends.

chapters.title: Ardeshir I — Founder of Sassan
chapters.summary: A herdsman's ambition, a court astrologer's prophecy, and a dynasty is born. Ardeshir refounds Pars.

chapters.title: Shapur the Great — Rome Kneels
chapters.summary: Two Roman armies captured. Shapur's name is carved in rock for eternity.

chapters.title: Bahram Gur — The Lion Hunter
chapters.summary: The lion hunter. The poet-king who rhymes his own legend. Bahram vanishes into the earth with his horse.

chapters.title: Yazdegerd the Sinner
chapters.summary: The king who earned the worst name in the chronicle. Cruelty breeds only its mirror.

chapters.title: Bahram Chubin — The Rebel
chapters.summary: The greatest general who dared to call himself king. His rebellion reshapes the Sassanian world.

chapters.title: Khosrow Anushirvan — The Just
chapters.summary: Courts poets, reforms the land, defeats the Hephthalites. The golden height of the Sassanians.

chapters.title: Nushzad — The Rebellious Prince
chapters.summary: The Christian son of the Just King rebels against his father — and is answered with iron.

chapters.title: Hormuz — The Crumbling Crown
chapters.summary: The son who squanders the father's legacy. The throne becomes the prize in a game of knives.

chapters.title: Khosrow Parviz — The Conqueror
chapters.summary: The conqueror of Jerusalem, collector of horses and marvels. His pride dims even the sun.

chapters.title: Shirin — Queen of Love
chapters.summary: Queen, lover, builder. Shirin's courage outlasts the empires around her.

chapters.title: The Crumbling Crown
chapters.summary: Fourteen rulers in thirty years. Civil war, betrayal, and plague. The Sassanian house devours itself.

chapters.title: Yazdegerd III — The Last King
chapters.summary: The last Sassanian king runs east with his treasury and no army. The chronicle watches him and weeps.

chapters.title: The Arab Conquest — Fire and Sword
chapters.summary: Qadisiyya and Nihavand. Two battles, two seasons, and a thousand years of Persian kingship ends.

chapters.title: The Mourning of Pars
chapters.summary: Ferdowsi names the grief. The fire temples are dark. But the language of Pars keeps burning in every verse.

chapters.title: Memory Over Sword
chapters.summary: What the sword cannot keep, words can. Ferdowsi's testament to the power of Persian memory.

chapters.title: Ferdowsi's Legacy
chapters.summary: Thirty years. Sixty thousand verses. A tomb in Tus. The Shahnameh outlives every king it describes.

chapters.title: The Final War — Ages End
chapters.summary: The chronicle closes where it began: with fire, with iron, with kings.
chapters.story: The chronicle closes where it began: with fire, with iron, with kings. Ferdowsi's verses outlive the empires they describe. What was once a kingdom of crystal becomes a kingdom of memory, and every reader joins the lineage of Pars.
